references.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

rows.label: match
rows.reason: Both identify the conflict between float:left on .login-button/.sign-up-button and the new flexbox layout in the parent .contents container, which is the same concrete layout issue.

rows.label: uncertain
rows.reason: The concern about removing float and margin-top on .badge-wrapper.bullet is a subjective visual regression risk rather than a demonstrable bug introduced by the diff; no concrete failure is proven.

rows.label: false_positive
rows.reason: The finding claims the mixin lacks input validation, which is a subjective/style concern, not a concrete bug. The actual concrete bugs in the mixin (wrong -ms-align-items property and -webkit-box-ordinal-group/moz-box-ordinal-group requiring 1-based values) are covered by references 1 and 2 but this finding does not diagnose either of those specific failures.
